Rello is a grocery delivery app. It delivers in fifteen minutes from small

A company does not answer to "the law". It answers to specific 
authorities. Each has its own instrument and its own powers.

FROM YOUR READING · FOUR KINDS O F AUT HORIT Y

Permitting authorities give permission with conditions. They can change, suspend or 
cancel it.

Competition agencies investigate market behaviour and can order changes.

Labour enforcers can be inspectors, prosecutors, or both.

Data regulators audit how data is used and can order it to stop. Each asks a different 
question. An answer sent to the wrong one is useless.

How to find the duty

Find the exact words that matter, and say what each 
one promises. "At their sole discretion" promises a 
free choice. "To route your deliveries" names one 
purpose. The scoring system breaks the first. The 
dashboard goes beyond the second.

Strong words close doors

"Sole", "solely", "only", "any": companies use these 
words to reassure. Later, the same words block the 
company's defence. What counts is how the reader 
understands the words, not what the product team 
meant.

If the company's system does the opposite of its 
document, the system is the evidence. The falling 
score shows the "free choice" was not free. 
Employment status is decided the same way: by the 
facts — who directs, who scores, what refusing costs 
— not by the label "partner".
